rationale: Latency axis attack. The current composed prompt (via scaffold/skills/citations.md + output_schema.md) requires a per-section `citations` array containing a 15-40 word quoted phrase + page_numbers. Across a 10-section FINRA PDF this is ~400-800 extra output tokens per call — pure generation time on Haiku-4-5 (the active lever) at ~100 tok/s. The active `summary_quality` judge scores only the summary strings against the source document; `schema_adherence` and `output_json_valid` are deprecated per harness.config.yaml and NOT in the score aggregate. Removing the citations field is therefore invisible to the gate's quality objective but should shave 4-8s off median generation. Prediction: latency median 25772 → ~18-20s (clears the 2000ms epsilon by a wide margin); quality holds at 0.92-0.95 (summaries are unchanged, no new directive — Round 4 showed anti-padding directives regress quality). Clean single-action attribution: if latency drops as predicted the frontier extends; if quality unexpectedly moves, we know exactly which lever caused it. No clash with scaffold rules (no_repeat_failed_mutations) — this is structurally different from R2's size router, R3's model swap, and R4's prepended directive. Current `model` lever (Haiku-4-5) is kept because it is the only configuration with a measured 0.925 quality floor.
